lessons.meaning: ~(으)리, commonly in ~(으)리라고, expresses a formal or literary prediction, intention or belief about what will happen.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it in formal writing, speeches and reported expectations, especially with 생각하다 or 믿다.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~리 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~으리 after another consonant; combine it with 라고 in the quoted prediction form.
examples: 마을 어르신들은 올해도 기원제가 열리리라고 생각하시겠지요
The village elders probably think that the prayer ceremony will be held again this year
야당의 반대가 심하지만 결국에는 법안이 통과되리라고 생각해요
The opposition is strong, but I think the bill will eventually pass
그 사상가는 현실보다는 이상적인 관념을 따르리라고 생각됩니다
It is thought that the thinker will follow idealistic ideas rather than reality
그 사람이 어떤 상황에서도 폭력에 동조하리라고 생각하지 않아요
I don’t think that person would ever sympathize with violence under any circumstances.
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: ~(으)려니: Settled Assumption
lessons.explanation: Practice for the HTSK Lesson 202 focus. The official lesson contains the complete explanation and additional examples.

cards.translation: I waited, figuring they would hand it out
cards.explanation:
~(으)려니 expresses an assumption or expectation that the speaker accepts, often with a resigned or matter-of-fact tone.

Use it when assuming a situation will be a certain way, sometimes as a basis for waiting or accepting what follows.

Attach ~려니 after a vowel or ㄹ stem and ~으려니 after another consonant, then use 생각하다 or the surrounding construction shown by HTSK.

cards.prompt: 사람도 별로 ___ 하고 나룻배를 탔는데 도착해 보니 사람이 많았어요
